summary: Game crashes when dispensing a shulker box from a dispenser - "java.lang.NullPointerException: Exception while ticking"
description: (1.16 Pre-Release 3) [^crash-2020-06-10_18.21.22-server.txt] Description: Exception while ticking java.lang.NullPointerException: Exception while ticking at bil.a(SourceFile:88) at gy.a(SourceFile:23) at gu.dispense(SourceFile:15) at bxc.a(SourceFile:89) at bxc.a(SourceFile:112) at cfi$a.a(SourceFile:865) at zd.b(SourceFile:596) at zd$$Lambda$3895/290764432.accept(Unknown Source) at bqn.b(SourceFile:84) at zd.a(SourceFile:351) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:873) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:813) at eox.a(SourceFile:93) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.v(SourceFile:672) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:256) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer$$Lambda$3883/2115162896.run(Unknown Source) at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-Release 3.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place a dispenser in the world.
4. Add a shulker box to the dispenser's inventory.
5. Activate the dispenser to dispense the shulker box.
6. Observe that the game crashes with a "java.lang.NullPointerException: Exception while ticking" error.
Observed Behavior: The game experiences a crash when a shulker box is dispensed from a dispenser, resulting in a java.lang.NullPointerException with the message "Exception while ticking." This issue occurs specifically in version 1.16 Pre-Release 3. The crash log indicates that the error originates from the method bil.a at line 88 in the source file, followed by a series of method calls that lead to the dispense method in gu at line 15. The stack trace reveals that the error propagates through various classes and methods, including bxc and cfi$a, ultimately affecting the main MinecraftServer class and causing the game to terminate unexpectedly. This behavior suggests that there is a problem with how the game handles the dispensing of shulker boxes, likely related to the internal state management during the tick process, which requires further investigation to identify the underlying cause and implement a fix.
Expected Behavior: When dispensing a shulker box from a dispenser, the game should successfully release the shulker box without any errors or crashes, allowing it to function as intended. The shulker box should drop into the world and be usable by players, maintaining its contents and properties. This expected behavior would ensure a smooth gameplay experience in Java Edition 1.16 Pre-Release 3 and beyond.
